blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — post-infusion safety monitoring for intravenous iron sucrose
stem: A client with CKD-related iron deficiency anemia receives an intravenous iron sucrose infusion. Which nursing action is most important after the infusion is completed?

options.A: Observe for hypersensitivity for at least 30 minutes and until clinically stable, while continuing to monitor for hypotension after the intravenous iron dose.
options.B: Discharge immediately after the infusion because serious hypersensitivity reactions generally occur only while iron sucrose is actively being administered.
options.C: Monitor mainly for hypoglycemia after the infusion because hypotension and serious hypersensitivity are not clinically important labeled risks of iron sucrose.
options.D: Obtain serum iron immediately after the infusion because the first post-dose hours provide the most accurate measurement of the client's iron status.

rationale: Current iron sucrose labeling requires monitoring for hypersensitivity during and after administration for at least 30 minutes and until the patient is clinically stable; serious-reaction personnel and therapies must be immediately available. The label also requires monitoring for hypotension following each administration. In addition, serum iron measurements should not be performed for at least 48 hours after IV dosing because transferrin saturation rises rapidly. Therefore A is correct. B and C ignore labeled risks, and D uses an explicitly inappropriate laboratory timing.
educational_objective: After IV iron sucrose, observe for hypersensitivity for at least 30 minutes and until clinically stable, continue hypotension monitoring, and avoid immediate serum-iron testing.
source_document_title: IRON SUCROSE injection — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: DailyMed updated June 5, 2026; prescribing information revised March 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §5.1 Hypersensitivity Reactions: monitor during and after administration for at least 30 minutes and until clinically stable. §5.2 Hypotension: monitor following each administration. §5.3 Iron Overload: do not perform serum iron measurements for at least 48 hours after IV dosing.
source_claim_supported: Iron sucrose requires at least 30 minutes of post-administration hypersensitivity observation until clinically stable, post-dose hypotension monitoring, and avoidance of serum-iron measurement for 48 hours.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: monitor adverse medication reactions, safely administer parenteral medications, interpret related laboratory findings, and intervene for complications.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices as complete post-infusion monitoring or laboratory actions of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the June 2026 iron-sucrose safety instructions. No absolute cue or second defensible post-infusion action remains.
